question: Does a sourceblind model over distinct public nonlinear composition grammars identify correct unobserved outputs under matched resource constraints, instead of relying on a single T6 affine slope?
source: Source-neutral negative cases -21000..-21011 only: three independently specified 4bit bijection classes: odd-affine mod16, affine XOR mask, and odd-affine XOR mask followed by 1bit nibble rotation. Common 3-round 16bit Sbox+rotate3. 40 public FIT, 8 CHECK with exactly six corrupted public outputs, 16 independent unseen evaluator-only inputs; no consumed T7 A/B or registered MNS cohorts.
candidate: Untrained universal compositional program parser enumerating family-specific candidate programs across three classes with common 8B Sbox representation, score by 40 public bit errors. Strongest exact exhaustive union-of-grammars matched. Include original T5 general 8B pair-swap, T8 learned slope prior where valid; measure all costs and whole-process peak separately.
controls: strongest full structural program grammar exhaustive search on identical FIT
unchanged T5 general permutation-fit on same inputs
prior T8 shared-slope model where grammar relevant
acceptance: Source-neutral diagnostic only; compare 12 cases exact held accuracy against exhaustive grammar and total CPU/peak. A perfect structural control prevents strict accuracy uplift. Cannot admit OOD science without equal or lower cost and independent prospective original new source families. Need failure-grounded representation revision, not count gates.
